title: Adaptive-capacity embedding plus token Mirror view
hypothesis: A per-token Mirror angle can restore useful function variation in frequency-banded low-dimensional embeddings, especially for rare tokens, while using no more complete bytes than an adaptive embedding with one additional physical latent coordinate per token.
physical_object: One frequency-banded token embedding code table with latent widths 16 for 64 frequent tokens, 8 for 128 medium tokens and 4 for 192 rare tokens, projected into a fixed 16-dimensional representation.
mirror_coordinate: One learned token-specific Givens angle rotates the first output feature pair after the shared band projection; it adds one scalar/token while retaining the original adaptive latent widths.
logical_multiplicity: 384 token embeddings with frequency-dependent physical widths and one additional functional view coordinate per token.
prior_art_delta: PA60 establishes adaptive capacity allocation by frequency. This experiment tests whether a token-level Mirror coordinate recovers useful function lost in the low-width bands, compared both to standard adaptive widths and to a byte-matched control that adds one ordinary latent coordinate per token.

methods: byte-matched adaptive embedding with widths 17/9/5 and no Mirror view
adaptive 16/8/4 codes plus one learned Mirror angle per token

teacher.basis: Each frequency band has a fixed seeded projection from its latent width to 16 output dimensions. Projection seeds are paid and deterministically reconstruct the projection matrices.
teacher.target: For each token, sample a latent vector at its registered band width and a seeded angle; project the vector and rotate its first 2D feature plane by that token angle. Teacher target labels use one fixed 16x16 decoder.
teacher.sampling: Train token examples from the registered band masses, uniform within each frequency band. Evaluate all tokens both uniformly and with registered sampling-mass weights.
teacher.purpose: Aligned feasibility probe: tests an explicitly frequency-dependent low-capacity embedding where the Mirror coordinate matches the teacher's functional orbit.

controls: adaptive 16/8/4 latent widths without per-token View
byte-matched simple adaptive 17/9/5 latent widths without View
adaptive 16/8/4 plus per-token Givens Mirror angle

development.selection_metric: Frequency-mass-weighted embedding NRMSE is primary; uniform/per-band embedding NRMSE, weighted decoder NLL/top-1, actual complete bytes, compute proxy and wall time are secondary.
development.allowed_tuning: No tuning planned; bands, teacher, optimizer and training schedule are fixed. Correctness-only changes rerun development before fresh access.

fresh.open_gate: Both development worlds: full NRMSE <=0.03; Mirror weighted NRMSE <=0.05 and weighted decoder NLL within .02 nat/top-1 within 1pp of full; Mirror actual payload <=0.60x full table; Mirror beats standard adaptive rare-band NRMSE by >=.05 and byte-matched adaptive weighted NRMSE by >=.01 at <=1.10x its actual payload; frequent-band Mirror degradation <=.03 NRMSE; exact serialized replay. Otherwise fresh stays sealed.
fresh.fresh_success: All three worlds meet all weighted, band-specific, byte-matched-control, full-table and replay gates.

storage.authority: actual compressed NPZ inference payload bytes after reload
paid_objects: full embedding or each band-specific latent code
each per-token Mirror angle or additional adaptive coordinates
band boundaries, dimensions, sampling metadata and deterministic projection seeds
archive names, headers and compression overhead
storage.deterministic_reconstruction: Projection matrices are regenerated from stored seeds and fixed algorithm; seed metadata is charged.

success_gate: All three fresh worlds satisfy weighted quality, rare-band recovery, byte-matched adaptive comparison, full-table compression and exact replay gates.
failure_gate: Any development quality, rare-band, byte-matched control, full-table storage or replay gate fails.
boundaries: synthetic frequency-banded embedding screen, not a language model or real Zipf corpus
projection bases are fixed random matrices, not learned frequency embeddings
the Mirror teacher is aligned to a 2D rotation orbit
fixed update budget is not near-convergence or capacity evidence
